terms.grammar: pronoun: the ordinary forms of nōs, used reflexively
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.6.2: ut nōbīsmet ipsīs … placeāmus
terms.comment: No separate reflexive; stressed, nōsmet, nōbīsmet, usually with ipsī. “Each other” among us is inter nōs.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 4.14: sī nōsmet ipsōs regere possumus (Lewis & Short, s.v. agō)
terms.comment: Agrees with nōs as subject (id nōsmet ipsōs facere oportet stresses us as the doers) or as object.

phrases.latin: nōs Tusculānō ita dēlectāmur ut nōbīsmet ipsīs tum dēnique cum illō vēnimus placeāmus
phrases.english: We love Tusculum so much that we are only pleased with ourselves when we have got there.

phrases.latin: Id nōsmet ipsōs facere oportet, Phaedria.
phrases.english: We have to do it ourselves, Phaedria.

phrases.latin: cāriōrem esse patriam nōbīs quam nōsmet ipsōs
phrases.english: that our country is dearer to us than our own selves

phrases.latin: agitur praeclārē, sī nōsmet ipsōs regere possumus
phrases.english: we do very well if we can govern ourselves

phrases.latin: ut nōsmet ipsī inter nōs conjūnctiōrēs sīmus
phrases.english: so that we ourselves may be closer to each other

sources: Lewis & Short: nos · Lewis & Short: ipse
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
